claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First of all, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 21 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex. Since Alex is 21 years old, I need to ask a few more questions to determine eligibility, as there are specific rules for children aged 16 and over.

Is Alex currently enrolled in any form of approved education or training? For example:
- Full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar)
- An approved training course (not paid for by an employer)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school a while back and hasn't gone on to do anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Unfortunately, based on what you've told me, it doesn't look like you would be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me explain why: Child Benefit can only be claimed for children who are either:
- Under 16 years old, or
- 16, 17, 18, 19, or 20 years old **and** in approved education or training

Since Alex is 21 and is not currently in approved education or training, he no longer meets the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

Before I give you my final assessment, may I just confirm: are you (or your partner, if applicable) responsible for Alex, and is he living with you in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - he lives here at home with me in the UK, and I'm responsible for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I appreciate you providing all the details.

Unfortunately, even though Alex lives with you in the UK and you are responsible for him, the age and education requirements are the key factors here. Since Alex is 21 years old and is not in approved education or training, he does not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

Child Benefit eligibility for someone over 16 requires them to be:
- Aged 16, 17, 18, 19, or 20 **and**
- In approved full-time education (non-advanced) or approved training

As Alex is 21, he has passed the maximum age for Child Benefit eligibility, regardless of his education status.

Let me now provide you with my formal assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, I'm sorry to confirm that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Summary:**
- **Alex (age 21):** Not eligible

**Reason:** Child Benefit can only be claimed for children under 16, or for those aged 16 to 20 who are in approved full-time education or training. Since Alex is 21 years old, he has exceeded the maximum age for Child Benefit, regardless of other circumstances.

I'm sorry this isn't the outcome you were hoping for. If you have any other questions or if your circumstances change in the future, please don't hesitate to ask.
